Built against [wamsoft/krkrz_dev](https://github.com/wamsoft/krkrz_dev) V2.6.5

- **A manual inside the game**: F1, Help > Contents or Config's Manual button opens pages of help on every platform: the controls, saving, the settings, and what to do when the game is slow, the picture is stretched or blurry, there's no sound or movies don't play. Links go between pages (Back, Forward, Contents), change a setting there and then, or open a screen; pages show the keys you've set. Games add their own pages
- **Two languages at once, and menus in a language of their own**: Config's Languages page shows a second language under each line, smaller (Shift+F9 swaps the two), and puts the menus in another language than the story
- **Objects that move with others**: a prop attached to a character moves, zooms, turns and leaves with it; a light can be clipped to a character's outline; a copy can follow a character's picture, blinking with it. The Character demo has a speech bubble on Pip, a light on Ai and a mirrored copy of her
- **Choices that change pictures later on**: a picture or an outfit can depend on an earlier choice, decided as it's drawn: take the park in the Character demo and Pip wears his beret later
- **CG variations from one layered file**: several CGs made from one Photoshop or CLIP STUDIO PAINT file's layers, each with its own name in the gallery; the Animated Character demo shows four of Pip's
- **Full screen part way**: Full Screen Fit's Part Way fills the screen by a percentage, between the bars and cutting the edges off. The Screen menu lists the window sizes that fit your screen
- For game makers: `tools/playtest.py` plays your game's routes on their own (every branch, several at once) and reports the first script error with its file, line and tag, or where it got stuck; the Debug menu restarts the script, goes to any line, shows and sets the flags (`flaglist.txt`), copies the voice's file name or where the game is, writes a bug report and traces every tag; `-scncompile` reports each language's texts still untranslated; `attach=`, `follow=`, `clipto=`, `relative=` (`KAGEnvLinks.tjs`); `cgvariations.txt` (`CGVariations.tjs`); manual pages (`manual_<page>.txt`, `Manual.tjs`); `-allseen=yes`
- kagex-release 0.26.0 downloads the 0.26.0 engines

The sample game with Live2D (`kagex_sample_live2d_<platform>`, added to this release once it's out) holds Live2D's Cubism Core: by installing or playing it you agree not to copy the Cubism Core out of it, distribute it apart from the game, modify it, or reverse engineer, decompile or disassemble it. It uses sample data owned and copyrighted by Live2D Inc.

Everything in this release is listed in [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/krkren/kagex/blob/0.26.0/CHANGELOG.md).

On Windows the engine needs OpenGL ES: a graphics driver that supports it, or ANGLE's `libEGL.dll` and `libGLESv2.dll` next to `krkrz.exe`.

The macOS app and tools aren't signed with an Apple Developer ID, so macOS blocks them the first time: open the app from the context menu (Open), or allow it under System Settings > Privacy & Security; for the tools, `xattr -d com.apple.quarantine kagex-release kagex-lipsync`. The Android APK is signed with a debug key: allow installs from unknown sources, or use `adb install`. The sample's iOS build is for the Simulator; kagex-release signs a game for iPhones and iPads with your own Apple Developer certificate.
